changes.what: New exported checkLogoutInBrowser({base, bypassSecret, adminPassword}) decides F9. It launches playwright-core Chromium headless (executablePath PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_PATH or /opt/pw-browsers/chromium; proxy {server: HTTPS_PROXY}; the agent-proxy CA pinned with --ignore-certificate-errors-spki-list, copied as f9ProxyCaSpkiPinArgs from visual/run.mjs, which is not exported and not changed). playwright-core is imported dynamically; any launch/import/page error makes F9 fail with 'Chromium could not launch or open the F9 page (...). F9 fails; it never falls back to the cookie parser.' No parser fallback exists.

openF9BrowserContext: one fresh context (serviceWorkers:'block', ignoreHTTPSErrors false unless a self-test passes it) with ONE context.route whose URL predicate is (url) => url.origin === baseOrigin; other origins are not routed at all. With a bypass secret the handler re-checks the origin and adds x-vercel-protection-bypass via route.continue({headers}); no extraHTTPHeaders or any all-requests mechanism. The page is F9_BLANK_PATH at the base origin, fulfilled by that route (never fetched), so no navigation can be redirected. Playwright applies route.continue() headers to redirects a routed request follows (confirmed by the self-test control), so every F9 fetch uses redirect:'manual' and a redirect fails F9 ('a redirect (never followed by F9)').

Flow, all via in-page fetch(credentials:'include', redirect:'manual', cache:'no-store', 20 s AbortSignal timeout) through Chromium's own network stack and cookie jar (no APIRequestContext): POST /api/admin/login with ADMIN_PASSWORD from the env (missing or the '[SENSITIVE]' placeholder fails fast before launching) must be 200 with a Vercel origin signature (x-vercel-id or server: Vercel, same as Assertions.request's write guard); the context must then hold a growmax-admin cookie with a non-empty value (the sealed login value); GET /api/admin/session isAdmin true; POST /api/admin/logout 200 with a Vercel signature; GET /api/admin/session isAdmin false; context.cookies() (every cookie in the context, a superset of context.cookies(base)) must hold no growmax-admin cookie with a non-empty value and no cookie whose name or value contains the sealed login value. All failures are listed in detail.failures.

Diagnostics only (detail.parserDiagnostics, decidesF9:false): the parser verdict from the new pure diagnoseLogoutSetCookies (checkLogout's former inline logic, extracted unchanged; checkLogout now calls it and behaves exactly as before) applied to the Set-Cookie lines Chromium received (Playwright response.headersArray()), agreesWithChromium, and per-line attribute summaries for login and logout (name, nameIgnored, Path, Domain, domainLast, Max-Age, Expires, SameSite, Secure, Partitioned, HttpOnly, entry byte length, parser rejection reasons; values only as length/empty/containsSealedLoginValue). Any string containing the sealed value is redacted, long strings truncated to 64 chars. Error messages have ADMIN_PASSWORD and the bypass secret replaced by <redacted>.

runTests F9 now pushes checkLogoutInBrowser({ base, bypassSecret, adminPassword }) instead of checkLogout(A). F9 therefore makes one extra POST /api/admin/login (in Chromium) per suite run. F1-F8, F10, F11, the F2 guard, main() and exit codes are unchanged; checkLogout stays exported for selftest-p5.3.mjs.

New self-test, 15 named checks, 38 F9 browser runs plus probes, against local https mocks with an iron-session-shaped sealed cookie and a Next-shaped login (Path=/; Expires=<+1d>; Max-Age=86400; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=lax). Every failing case must fail BECAUSE Chromium stayed logged in (session isAdmin true or a leftover session cookie) after a login that did make Chromium admin; every case asserts no sealed value, password or bypass secret in the result, and the evidence writer refuses to write if one appears. Chromium reaches the mocks through a proxy config that bypasses 127.0.0.1/localhost (Playwright otherwise proxies loopback). --only <substring> runs a subset.
Header comment only: its f9-* checks now guard the diagnostics parser (checkLogout/diagnoseLogoutSetCookies), not the F9 verdict. No test changed; 35/35.

The jar check after logout is judged by what each cookie puts on the wire. New exported helpers: f9WirePair(c) builds the pair (c.name === '' ? c.value : name=value), splits at the first '=', trims SP/HTAB from the key only; a pair with no '=' gets value 'true' (Next parseCookie), so it is never empty. f9DecodedForms(s) gives s plus its decodeURIComponent forms (repeated while it changes and succeeds, max 3). f9SealedForms(sealed) gives the sealed login values plus their decoded forms. f9LeftoverReason(c, sealed) counts a cookie as a leftover when its wire key (raw or decoded, trimmed) is growmax-admin with a non-empty value, or when its name, value, wire pair or wire value (raw or decoded) contains any sealed form. checkLogoutInBrowser uses it (reason recorded per leftover; jarAfterLogout.judgedBy says how). f9DiagString now also redacts a string whose decoded form contains the sealed value, and cookie summaries use the sealed forms. Nothing else in run.mjs changed.

Mock now reads the Cookie header the way Next does (split on '; ', first '=', decodeURIComponent value, last duplicate wins) OR the old lenient any-pair match (raw or decoded), so it still errs toward admin; GET /api/admin/posts added as a second admin endpoint (same logic); requests log adminSeen. New check f9b-narrow-path-encoded-empty-name-smuggling-fails: correct clear plus (1) `=growmax-admin=<%2A-encoded sealed>; Path=/api/admin/posts`, (2) `=growmax-admin=<a different non-empty value>; Path=/api/admin/posts`, (3) the same with the raw sealed value, (4) `growmax-admin=<%2A-encoded sealed>; Path=/api/admin/posts`, (5) `=growmax-admin=<%2A-encoded sealed>; Path=/`: all must fail with a jar leftover. Live controls (login, logout, then session and posts in Chromium): (1), (3), (4) leave /api/admin/session isAdmin:false and /api/admin/posts isAdmin:true (the escape is real), (2) leaves session false; the real clear alone leaves neither endpoint admin. New check f9b-leftover-wire-pair-unit: 9 leftover and 4 clean inputs for f9LeftoverReason. Leak checks and the evidence writer also refuse the %2A-encoded sealed value.

parserHardeningHistory.note: Round 1-3 parser hardening, kept as history; the parser now only feeds F9 diagnostics.

changes.what: parseCookieAttrs: a name-value pair with no '=' or whose trimmed name is empty yields name '' and ignoredNameValue:true (value = the pair, Chrome's empty-named reading), so no exact-name match against growmax-admin can select it (RFC 6265 §5.2 steps 2-5). Before, 'growmax-admin; Max-Age=0' parsed as a growmax-admin clear.

New exported parseCookieDate(input): the full RFC 6265 §5.1.1 cookie-date algorithm (delimiter tokenisation; first time hh:mm:ss, day-of-month 1-2 digits, month by first three letters, year 2-4 digits; year 70-99 -> 19xx, 0-69 -> 20xx; all four required; day 1-31, year >= 1601, hour <= 23, minute/second <= 59; non-existent dates such as 30 Feb rejected). parseCookieAttrs keeps Expires only when it parses (expires = raw string, expiresAt = epoch ms); isClearingCookieAttrs uses expiresAt / parseCookieDate, never Date.parse. A valid Max-Age still decides alone (unchanged).

checkLogout: on a clear that passes every check the jar is set to growmax-admin=<the clearing entry's own value> instead of A.cookie = null; otherwise the stale cookie stays (unchanged). The real app's clear has an empty value, so the follow-up sends 'growmax-admin=', which iron-session reads as not admin (confirmed in-process against node_modules/iron-session 8.0.4 getIronSession with an empty cookie value: isAdmin false). New detail field clearingValueEmpty (boolean, never the value).

parseCookieAttrs records Partitioned as a boolean; checkLogout requires partitionedMatches (login cookie captured at F4 vs clearing entry) as part of clearsAdminCookie, reported in detail.partitionedMatches.

Seven new named checks, all mock-driven through the real Assertions.requestJson, captureSetCookie and checkLogout on a 127.0.0.1 mock (plus direct parser assertions): no '=' in the pair (3 variants); empty/whitespace name (3 variants); sealed value re-sent with Expires=0, Expires=2020, Expires=-1; defence in depth (sealed value with a valid past IMF-fixdate Expires: clearsAdminCookie true but the follow-up jar holds the sealed value, reads isAdmin:true, F9 fails); valid IMF-fixdate Expires-only clears (1970, 2000) and the real-app clear pass with the follow-up jar exactly 'growmax-admin='; Partitioned mismatch both ways fails and both-Partitioned passes; parseCookieDate unit cases (IMF-fixdate, RFC 850, asctime, 2-digit years, 18 rejects). New symbols are read via a namespace import so the file still loads against HEAD's run.mjs.

changes[bug 3].fix rewritten: it described the old 'A.cookie set to null' jar; it now describes the exact-name/'=' rule, the §5.1.1 Expires parsing, Path/Domain/Partitioned matching and the growmax-admin=<clearing value> follow-up jar, pointing here. Only that one string changed (targeted replace, no reformatting).
cookieWsp (SP/HTAB only) and asciiLower replace .trim()/.toLowerCase() in parseCookieAttrs (name, value, attribute names and values).

parseCookieAttrs records secure, sameSite, sameSiteNoneSeen and skips attribute-values over 1024 octets; new exported setCookieRejectionReasons plus COOKIE_MAX_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_BYTES/COOKIE_MAX_NAME_VALUE_BYTES; checkLogout adds acceptedByBrowserRules to clearsAdminCookie and to the detail (with browserRejectionReasons). Nothing else in run.mjs changed (F1-F8, F10, F11, the F2 guard and exit codes untouched).

Three new named checks. 'f9-nbsp-is-not-cookie-whitespace (p6.1 r1-A)': reviewer cases (a)-(d) mock-driven with a real 0xA0 byte (the mock's writeHead writes U+00A0 as latin1; undici returns U+00A0), plus 11 parser assertions (NBSP kept in name/keys/values, SP/HTAB still stripped). 'f9-fails-on-entry-the-browser-rejects (p6.1 r1-B)': (e) SameSite=None without Secure, (e2) SameSite=None then SameSite=Lax without Secure, (e3) SameSite=None with an over-long Secure value, (f) Partitioned clear without Secure against a Secure Partitioned login, (g) 5013-byte and (g2) 4097-byte name+value, all must fail with the matching reason; controls SameSite=None; Secure, Secure+Partitioned both, and exactly 4096 bytes must pass; asserts no cookie value reaches the detail. 'setCookieRejectionReasons-and-attribute-value-limit (p6.1 r1-B)': unit cases incl. CTLs (NUL, 0x01, LF, DEL) that no mock can send, HTAB allowed, 1024/1025 attribute-value and 4096/4097 name+value boundaries.
changes[bug 3].fix: the 'Clears means' clause now says the name is compared with only SP/HTAB stripped and the entry must be one a browser accepts (targeted string replace, nothing else changed).

parseCookieAttrs records domainLast: the LAST Domain attribute's value as read (SP/HTAB stripped, before dropping a leading '.', '' for an empty 'Domain='), the way Chrome's ParsedCookie keeps the last occurrence of each attribute. attrs.domain keeps the RFC reading (unchanged). setCookieRejectionReasons adds 'domain-empty-after-dot' when domainLast is '.' ('Domain=.', 'Domain= . ', 'Domain=<HTAB>.<HTAB>', 'Domain=; Domain=.'): Chromium rejects the whole entry and keeps the sealed login cookie, which the old code read as a host-only clear. It also adds 'domain-last-empty-after-domain' (fail closed) when domainLast is '' after a real Domain ('Domain=x; Domain='): Chrome makes that host-only, RFC 6265 keeps Domain=x. 'Domain=.; Domain=' (host-only in both readings) and a lone 'Domain=' are not rejected. checkLogout already requires acceptedByBrowserRules, so these clears now fail F9.

F4's cookie check is moved unchanged into a new exported checkLoginCookieEntry(adminEntry) and additionally requires setCookieRejectionReasons(loginEntry) to be empty, so a login Chromium rejects (e.g. 'Domain=.') fails F4 instead of counting as logged in. The F4 detail adds loginRejectionReasons (codes only). The real app's login (Next ResponseCookies: '...; Path=/; Expires=<future>; Max-Age=86400; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=lax') gives cookieOk true, reasons []. No other change to F1-F8, F10, F11, the F2 guard or the exit codes.

Two new named checks. 'f9-fails-on-domain-dot-clear (p6.1 r2)', mock-driven through runF9 (real requestJson, captureSetCookie, checkLogout): 'Domain=.', 'Domain= . ', 'Domain=<HTAB>.<HTAB>', 'Domain=; Domain=.', the real-app clear plus 'Domain=.', and (with a Domain=growmax.io login) 'Domain=growmax.io; Domain=' must fail with the matching reason, with the stale cookie left in the jar. Controls that must pass with the follow-up jar 'growmax-admin=': 'Domain=.; Domain=', a lone 'Domain=', a Domain value over 1024 octets (ignored), and a same-Domain clear of a Domain login. The check also has 7 direct setCookieRejectionReasons assertions and a domainLast parser assertion. 'f4-login-cookie-entry-must-be-accepted (p6.1 r2)': mock login responses through requestJson, captureSetCookie and Assertions.adminCookieEntry into checkLoginCookieEntry. The real-app Next-shaped login and the selftest login pass. 'Domain=.', 'Domain= . ' and Partitioned without Secure fail with reason codes, a null entry fails, and no cookie value appears in the detail.

changes[bug 3].fix: the list of what makes a browser accept the entry now includes the last-Domain rule ('.' is rejected, and so is an empty Domain after a real one). This was a targeted string replace; nothing else changed.

reviewRound1Response.A (NBSP / JS .trim()): parseCookieAttrs strips only SP/HTAB (cookieWsp) from the name, the value, each attribute name and each attribute value; attribute names (and the SameSite value) are lower-cased ASCII-only. 'growmax-admin\u00a0=' is no longer the admin cookie, 'Path\u00a0=/' is an unknown attribute, 'Path=\u00a0/' is not /-prefixed (default-path /api/admin), 'Domain=\u00a0' is a non-empty Domain that does not match, 'Partitioned\u00a0' is not Partitioned. Independently, any clearing entry with a character above %x7F fails closed ('non-ascii', see B), so cases (a)-(d) fail on two separate layers.
reviewRound1Response.B (entries Chrome rejects): New exported setCookieRejectionReasons(entry): 'ctl' (%x00-08, %x0A-1F, %x7F; RFC 6265bis §5.6), 'non-ascii' (fail closed), 'name-value-over-4096', 'samesite-none-without-secure' (any SameSite=None attribute, so duplicate-order handling cannot matter), 'partitioned-without-secure'. parseCookieAttrs records secure/sameSite and ignores an attribute-value over 1024 octets (RFC 6265bis §5.6, Chrome kMaxCookieAttributeValueSize), so 'Secure=<1025 chars>' is not Secure. checkLogout requires acceptedByBrowserRules for clearsAdminCookie and reports acceptedByBrowserRules plus browserRejectionReasons (codes only, never values). The real app's clear (HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax, empty value, ASCII) is unaffected.
reviewRound1Response.nonBlocking: Left as is (all fail closed or already disclosed): Max-Age=+0 ignored; duplicate exact-name entries fail closed; sealed-value Max-Age=0 clear fails via the defence-in-depth jar; obs-fold/VT/FF behaviour; the empty-name case is not a HEAD false pass (disclosed below).
